rows: An {initiating_actor} with a valued {relationship} asks for help fulfilling an {obligation} that conflicts with another priority.
The request is understandable even if compliance is difficult.
What does refusal or compromise mean for the relationship?
The friend reveals why they believed no one else could help.
What do they actually need versus what they asked for?
A {rival} asks for help with a {threat} that could later affect everyone.
Helping may strengthen the rival; refusing may let the shared problem grow.
What advantage changes hands through cooperation?
The rival offers information that can be verified only by helping.
A Shared History Has a Missing Piece
A {relationship} is disrupted when new {evidence} changes the understood story of {past_event}.
Different members immediately draw incompatible conclusions.
What present relationship depends on the old story?
Another hidden decision from the same period surfaces.
What does the new evidence actually prove?
A respected {initiating_actor} who normally provides guidance is unable to handle a problem involving {target}.
Their failure becomes visible to someone who depends on their reputation.
What changes when the mentor is no longer the reliable authority?
The mentor asks that part of the problem remain private.
Is the failure temporary, moral, practical or informational?
Who is ready to replace them?
A {rival} from {past_event} returns seeking a different relationship than before.
Their behavior supports the change, but their incentives remain complicated.
What is risked by trust, distrust or conditional cooperation?
Someone harmed by the rival rejects reconciliation.
Two allied actors each ask for support in mutually incompatible ways.
Neither request is obviously illegitimate or malicious.
What does each ally interpret as loyalty?
A compromise becomes possible only if both sides accept a loss.
The Person Being Protected Wants Out
An {affected_actor} dependent on protection, patronage or care rejects the arrangement.
Their desired independence exposes them to a real {threat} but also addresses a genuine grievance.
Who gets to define acceptable risk?
A third party offers independence on manipulative terms.
What part of the arrangement is protective versus controlling?
An Ally Is Missing at the Worst Time
A trusted {initiating_actor} fails to appear for an important shared {obligation}.
Their absence could mean betrayal, coercion, crisis or simple impossibility.
What must others decide before the ally's reason is known?
What would make them break the commitment?
Two actors who should have little reason to cooperate develop a meaningful {relationship}.
The bond immediately complicates an existing conflict or obligation.
Who feels threatened or betrayed by the new bond?
The relationship creates access to previously separated groups.
What expectations are others projecting onto the bond?
A Trusted Person Vouches for a Stranger
An {initiating_actor} stakes their reputation on a {new_arrival} the characters do not know.
The newcomer immediately needs access, help or protection that trust would normally have to earn.
What happens to the sponsor's reputation if trust is misplaced?
The stranger proves helpful while concealing something unrelated.
What can be verified without betrayal?
A piece of {evidence} reveals part of a hidden pattern involving {target} but leaves the most important connection unresolved.
A second clue can be pursued through more than one route.
What changes if the pattern is understood before others notice it?
A plausible false interpretation gains support.
What is missing from the pattern?
Who created or preserved the evidence?
An {initiating_actor} voluntarily admits involvement in {past_event} but denies the expected motive or consequence.
Their confession is specific enough to verify in part.
What current decision changes if the confession is accepted?
Verification proves one detail and contradicts another.
A Familiar Place Contains Something Unfamiliar
A hidden area or layer is discovered within {location} where people believed the layout was known.
Its contents imply deliberate concealment rather than simple neglect.
What changes if the hidden space becomes public?
Someone arrives who already knows it exists.
Why was it left discoverable at all?
The Official Story Cannot Fit the Evidence
New {evidence} contradicts a widely accepted account of {past_event}.
The contradiction is narrow but consequential enough that someone wants it contained.
What institutions, identities or agreements rest on the official account?
More evidence suggests the falsehood protected someone as well as deceived others.
The Message Was Not Meant for You
The characters receive {evidence} intended for a different {affected_actor}.
The contents are urgent enough that ignoring them is also a choice with consequences.
What duty, danger or opportunity follows from accidental knowledge?
The intended recipient starts searching for the missing message.
Who else knows it was intercepted?
Someone Has Been Helping in Secret
A pattern of unexplained advantages around {affected_actor} suggests a hidden helper.
One new intervention carries a cost or message that makes the pattern impossible to ignore.
The helper's actions conflict with the beneficiary's values.
Previously unusable {evidence} becomes readable or interpretable after a new event.
The revealed portion references a {target} no one expected to be connected.
What new action or question becomes possible?
Only part of the material can be decoded before another condition is met.
Evidence reveals an undisclosed {relationship} between actors whose public positions imply distance or opposition.
The relationship may be benign, manipulative or mutually protective.
What decisions were made under the assumption they were unconnected?
A third actor knows the relationship and interprets it differently.
What does each person believe the relationship means?
An {affected_actor} with direct knowledge of {past_event} becomes reachable again.
Their testimony challenges both the official account and a popular alternative.
What current conflict changes if the witness is believed?
Someone attempts to discredit or protect the witness before full testimony.
A Secret Exists, But Nobody Claims It
A hidden {target} or piece of {evidence} is discovered without a clear owner, author or intended recipient.
Several actors have reasons to claim it after learning it exists.
Who gains control over interpretation by claiming ownership?
A claim is supported by real evidence but may still be incomplete.
Was it meant to be found?
